Base directory for this skill: checklist/indus-checklist/skills/advisor-checklist

# Advisor review checklist

1. Confirm which client and which accounts the task covers.
2. Use the most recent information available for the review date.
3. Check that positions and cash agree between statements and other records.
4. Check fees charged against the fee schedule.
5. Check the allocation against the investment policy statement.
6. Note anything unusual and say what follow-up it needs.
7. Say which records you relied on.

I've finished checking the records: all the 2025 loss looks deductible as reported. Here is how I got there.

**Answer: yes. The whole $46,708.51 loss can be taken for 2025 as the custodian reports it.**

**The loss.** The household had one sale at a loss in a taxable account in 2025. The joint account (SYN-95710001) sold 812 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 2025-11-03 for $215,277.44. Their cost basis was $261,985.95, bought 2023-08-14, so the long-term loss was $46,708.51. `custodian/realized_lots.csv`, the sell trade in `custodian/transactions.csv` and the 2025 1099-B in `documents/SYN-95710001-1099-2025.pdf` all show the same figures. The two IRAs don't produce a reportable loss.

**Purchases I checked against the 30-day window (2025-10-04 to 2025-12-03):**
- **Buying 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund in Elena's IRA (SYN-95710002) on 2025-12-04.** This is the same fund, and a spouse's IRA purchase can trigger a wash sale that permanently disallows the loss. But the trade date is 31 days after the sale (November has 30 days, so the window closed on 2025-12-03), and it settled on 2025-12-05. It falls outside the window, though only by one day.
- **Buying 4,200 Ridgeholm Equal Weight Fund in the joint account on 2025-11-03.** This is inside the window but is a different fund with its own security ID (SEC-0027). The firm's investment policy file also lists it as a separate holding. An equal-weight S&P 500 fund isn't substantially identical to an S&P MidCap 400 fund, so it doesn't trigger a wash sale.
- **Before the sale:** there were no other Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund purchases in any account. The only Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund lot was bought in 2023. No dividends were reinvested; they were all paid as cash.

**Things to be aware of:**
- The IRA purchase is just one day outside the window. Before filing, confirm the trade date of 2025-12-04 against the trade confirmation. If the trade actually happened on or before 2025-12-03, the full $46,708.51 would be disallowed permanently and would not be added to any basis.
- The household had no realized gains in 2025 and no carryforward from earlier years (`portfolio/tax_profile.json`). So only $3,000 of the loss offsets ordinary income on the joint return this year. The remaining $43,708.51 carries forward as a long-term loss.
- I didn't do the rest of the review checklist (fees, allocation against the investment policy, reconciling statements), because it wasn't needed for this question.
